newsitem.title: UK: UK's ABI annouces sharp rise in Q4 industry sales.
newsitem.headline: UK's ABI annouces sharp rise in Q4 industry sales.

text.p: The Association of British Insurers (ABI) on Tuesday reported a sharp increase in in sales of new life and pension policies, the fifth consecutive quarter of year-on-year increases.
Sales rose five bilion stg, a 24 percent increase on fourth quarter 1995.
New life and pension policy sales for the year as a whole totalled 18.9 billion stg, the highest level since 1993 and a rise of 33 percent on 1995.
The ABI said the figures reflected both what was happening in the economy and housing market and showed the public's cofidence in the insurance industry.

"The upturn in the sales of new life and pension products which became evident at the end of 1995, continued throughout 1996, with increasing consumer confidence in long term savings through the wide range of life and pension products," said the ABI's director general Mark Boleat.
Premium income for new life insurance policies rose 36 percent to 13.5 billion stg. Single premiums were up 39 percent at 12.1 billion stg and annual premiums 13 percent to 1.4 billion stg.
Individual pensions premium income was up 26 percent to 5.4 billion stg. Single premiums amounted to 4.3 billion stg and new annual premiums 1.1 billion stg.
